gap: No result ChatGPT got states the mechanism in the makers' words: noise cancelling needs the ear canal sealed. Soundcore tells Liberty 4 Pro owners to 'achieve a tight seal' and run the Fit Test. Bose says 'Due to the open-ear design, the earbuds do not include active noise cancelling.' The only open-style buds that cut noise do it by closing in on the ear and losing battery life: AeroFit 2 Pro runs ANC only with both hooks at levels 4–5, 'semi-in-ear', 5 h vs 7 h; OpenFit Pro gives 6 h with noise reduction vs 12 h without.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no result pages, so there is no cited rival page. Its own answer comes closest: its table says open-ear has 'Usually none' noise cancellation and is 'Poor in noise' for office or plane. It gives no reason (no ear seal), no source, and no mention of the hybrid models (Soundcore AeroFit 2 Pro, Shokz OpenFit Pro) or what they cost you in battery life.
decides: This confirms the split rather than changing it. If the shopper needs quiet on a subway, a plane or in a loud gym, a pure open-ear model (AeroFit 2, AeroClip 2, OpenFit 2, Bose Ultra Open) cannot give it, because none of them seals the ear. Pick a sealed in-ear bud such as the Liberty 4 Pro. A buyer who wants open-ear most of the time but sometimes needs quiet should get a hybrid: the AeroFit 2 Pro ($179.99) turns ANC on only in its semi-in-ear hook position at 5 h per charge, and the OpenFit Pro ($249.95) halves its battery to 6 h with noise reduction on. Shokz claims an average 14 dB reduction for the OpenFit Pro. Also, our page's Bose link returns 404. The current Bose model is the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) at $299, with 9 h plus 19.5 h from the case and IPX4, so that row needs updating.
